newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude trades sharply lower, other grades hit.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude trades sharply lower, other grades hit.

text.p: Dated Brent traded sharply weaker on Monday and differentials for other North Sea grades softened as a handful of late September cargoes struggled to find buyers, traders said.
A Sept 20-22 Brent was sold to a U.K. refiner at Oct Brent less 47 cents a barrel, 10 cents below late Friday talk and 12-15 cents cheaper than trades last Thursday.
Other late September barrels still unsold were in the hands of two Wall Street refiners and a European major, traders said.
"There are still several cargoes at the end of September and not too much demand showing," said a trader.
Outright Nov Brent was off 71 cents at $22.42 a barrel by 1730 GMT, under pressure from an easing of tension in the Middle East which helped drive the market to five-year highs last week.
Brent spreads lost 10 cents with Nov/Dec trade at +62 cents.
Sellers of other North Sea grades were struggling to place early October barrels with so much September Brent still unsold.
"It's tough placing barrels in the Oct 1-10 period. I don't see many buyers willing to pay up and there are too many Brents around looking for homes," said a Norwegian seller.
Early October Statfjord and Ekofisk slipped five cents, with offers coming from Dated +25 and +20 cents respectively.
Urals in the Med held its value on Monday, despite a very weak price for a distressed cargo, traders said.
A cargo loading on September 17-19 in Odessa was finally sold at Dated Brent -90 cents cif Augusta, but later loadings held onto their Dated -80/-75 cents value.

A trader said the market was well supported and prices hinged on maintenance of Novorossiisk's main pipeline later this week. The 90,000 tonnes per day line is due to stop for repairs for four days from September 20.
Sweet crude prices were also steady in the Med, with more West African imports offsetting stronger demand.
